bets.summary: Oregon (3-2) is a 7-point home favorite over Nebraska (5-1), total 51.5, but QB Dante Moore (concussion) is OUT again and Oregon has not named a starter between Dylan Raiola (6/19, 43 yds, 2 INT vs UCLA) and Brock Thomas. Nebraska's defense allows 15.2 ppg; player props are excluded (Ohio ban), so the legs are game, team-total and first-half lines.

legs.note: Without Moore, Oregon scored 15 points against UCLA, and Nebraska allows 15.2 ppg with no opponent above 23. Dimers projects Oregon for 30, so the market and models sit near the number, but the backup-QB evidence leans under.

legs.note: Martinez allows about 7 hits per 9 innings (1.09 WHIP), and the market expects about 12 outs from him. That projects around 3 hits, so he needs a bad night to allow 4.

bets.summary: No. 5 Indiana (6-0, 22-game win streak) hosts No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) at noon on FOX as roughly a 3-3.5 point home underdog with a total of 50.5; SP+ projects a 26-26 tie. Ohio State's injury list has six players out, including starting OT Austin Siereveld (now out, second straight game missed) and RB Ja'Kobi Jackson, plus five questionable players such as RB Isaiah West. Player props are dropped (Ohio bans college player props); the legs cover the side, OSU team total, first half and the game total.

legs.note: Price -110 at BetMGM, fair 0.503. SP+ projects 26-26, Indiana is at home on a 22-game win streak, Ohio State is without OT Siereveld and RB Ja'Kobi Jackson, and Covers, Yahoo, BUSR and TheSpread all lean Indiana; the OSU ML drifting from about -180 to -150 also points Indiana's way.

bets.summary: Florida (4-2, two straight losses) is expected to start sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. (first career start) at No. 7 Texas (4-1), with Aaron Philo (shoulder) questionable; reports (On3/Nakos, CBS/Zenitz, Saturday Down South) point to Jones, but there was no official pregame confirmation as of this check. The market already moved toward Texas -11 and a total of 51.

legs.note: A first-start QB tends to be most limited early, before adjustments, so a first-half under fits the same thesis with a modest lean.

bets.summary: Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor (turf toe) was downgraded to doubtful and is not expected to play per ESPN's Pete Thamel; freshman Parker 'Billy' Puckett would start, and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell is also doubtful. The market already moved hard on this (LSU -11.5/-14 to -17.5, total 58.5-59.5 to 56), so edges are modest; best lean is the Mississippi State team total under.

legs.desc: Mississippi State Bulldogs team total Under 19.5
legs.note: A freshman backup QB (3-for-6, 26 yds in relief vs Alabama) without lead RB Bothwell faces an LSU defense allowing about 176 pass ypg with nearly 4 sacks a game; pre-news models projected MSST around 23 with Taylor. Garbage-time points and LSU turnovers (Leavitt pick-six vs La Tech) are the main risk.

bets.summary: SMU (4-1, off a bye, 3-0 at Ford Stadium) hosts Virginia (4-2) with SP+ projecting SMU 30-23 and FPI giving Virginia about 31%, roughly in line with the market's -8.5 to -10 spread and 51.5 total. The clearest angle is SMU's passing offense (Jennings 317.6 yds/g) against a Virginia secondary missing CB Omillio Agard for the season, with both starting safeties doubtful.

legs.note: Jennings averages 317.6 pass yds/g, and Virginia is missing CB Agard (out for the season) with safeties Costner and Hillman doubtful, so SMU should be able to throw. Against that, SP+ projects SMU for exactly 30 points, and SMU managed only 218 yards against BC before the bye, so this is a modest lean.

bets.summary: No. 6/7 Alabama (5-1) is a -7.5/-8 road favorite at No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) with the total down from about 56.5 to 51; Tennessee starts backup-turned-starter George MacIntyre (Faizon Brandon questionable, shoulder) while Alabama is without WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, C Racin Delgatty and five defenders. Tennessee's defense (15.5 ppg, 4.7 yds/play, 161 pass ypg, nation-leading 25 sacks) against Alabama's leaky pass protection (113th in sacks allowed) is the main matchup.

legs.desc: Alabama Crimson Tide team total Under 30.5
legs.note: Alabama averages 44.2 ppg, but Tennessee's defense allows 15.5 ppg and leads the nation in sacks, and Alabama is missing its top WR and starting center against that pass rush. This is the same thesis as the dropped Russell passing under, expressed as a team total.

bets.summary: No. 13 Missouri (5-1) visits No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1) at homecoming. Ole Miss is a 5.5-point favorite, down from 6, with the total at 58.5. Missouri's top-25 defense (16.6 ppg, 78 rush ypg allowed) and SEC-leading rusher Jamal Roberts (828 yds, 138/g) face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the SEC (176 ypg allowed). Both starting QBs are healthy: Simmons was taken off the injury report, and Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy is out. Ohio bans college football player props, so only game, team-total and first-half lines are proposed.

legs.note: Roberts (138 rush ypg, SEC leader) faces the SEC's worst run defense (176 ypg allowed, 68 missed tackles), and Ole Miss's defense ranks 72nd in yards per play. The -125 price, Hardy's absence and Missouri's slow, clock-draining pace (27 points vs Texas A&M) limit the edge.

bets.summary: No. 2-3 Notre Dame (6-0, 4-2 ATS) visits No. 8 BYU (5-0 SU and ATS) at night with College GameDay in town. BYU is without RB LJ Martin. ND CB Leonard Moore (concussion) is questionable but practicing, and DT Jason Onye (ankle) is questionable. The market is ND -10.5 at about a coin flip, with the total down from 48.5 to 46.5.

legs.note: Without LJ Martin, BYU's run-first offense (224 rush ypg) faces the No. 1 total defense in FBS, which is 3rd against the run, and the market already shades this side (fair 0.534). BYU does score 34.6 ppg at home with a mobile QB, so the case is for a modest lean, not a strong edge.

bets.summary: No. 12 UCLA (5-0, 5-0 ATS) hosts Wisconsin (4-1, off a bye) at night in the Rose Bowl, with backup Ty Dieffenbach (Cal Poly transfer, 3/6 for 43 yds in relief) making his first UCLA start because Nico Iamaleava has a leg injury that is expected to end his season. The market has moved toward Wisconsin (spread from 3 to 2.5) and the Under (total from 44.5 to 42.5-43.5), and most Action Network experts back Wisconsin +3.

legs.note: A new QB making his first start and two run-first, clock-controlling offenses point to a slow first half; 21.5 is about half of the 43 full-game total, so the edge is thin and comes from the same factors as the full-game Under.

bets.summary: No. 15 Kentucky (5-1, four straight wins incl. OT upsets of South Carolina and LSU) visits 3-2 Oklahoma, which just beat No. 1 Texas 27-24 on an elite defense (about 238 ypg allowed) but a sputtering offense (10, 14, 13, 27 vs FBS opponents). The market (OU -6.5, total 43.5) looks efficient; the only lean is the Oklahoma team total under 24.5.

legs.note: Kentucky has scored at least 31 in every game except Alabama (17), with almost no turnovers, but Oklahoma's defense allows about 17.6 ppg and held Michigan, UNM and Texas to 24 or fewer. Close to fair.
